title: Capacity & Volume
subject: Mathematics
description: Measure liquids in litres and millilitres, and compare volume
nscObjectives: Explore and measure capacity in litres
Know that liquids are measured in litres and millilitres
Compare the volume of liquids in containers

sections.name: Litres and Millilitres
sections.instruction: Liquids are measured in litres and millilitres. We write L for litre and ml for millilitre.

questions.prompt: Liquids are measured in litres and ___.
questions.hint: Litres for big amounts, millilitres for small amounts.

questions.prompt: What is the short form for litre?
questions.hint: We write L for litre and ml for millilitre.

questions.prompt: What instrument do we use to measure liquids?
questions.hint: The liquid measuring cup measures liquids.

questions.prompt: How many liquid measuring cups make 1 litre?

sections.name: What is Measured in Litres
sections.instruction: Litres are used to measure liquids like water, milk and juice — not solid things.

questions.prompt: Which of these can be measured in litres?
questions.hint: Litres measure liquids. Water is a liquid.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT measured in litres?
questions.hint: Flour is a dry solid — it is not a liquid.

questions.prompt: Which unit best measures a big bottle of soda?
questions.hint: Soda is a liquid, so we use litres.

questions.prompt: Select ALL the things measured in litres.
questions.hint: Pick the liquids — the things you can pour.

sections.name: Comparing Volume
sections.instruction: The amount of liquid in a container is called its volume. More liquid means more volume.

questions.prompt: Bottle A has 2 cups of water. Bottle B has 5 cups. Which has MORE water?
Put in order from LEAST to MOST: 7L, 9L, 5L, 6L, 4L.
questions.hint: Least means smallest first: start with 4L.

questions.prompt: A bucket has 5 litres of lemonade. A jug has 2 litres. Which has the GREATER volume?
Which is the GREATEST volume: 5L, 2L, 3L, or 9L?
questions.hint: The greatest is the biggest number of litres.

sections.name: Litre Word Problems
sections.instruction: Read carefully and decide whether to add or subtract the litres.

questions.prompt: There were 75L of juice in a pail. 50L was given away. How many litres are left?
Mr. Jones sold 56L of milk on Monday and 68L on Tuesday. How much MORE was sold on Tuesday?
A tank had 38L of water. Ivan added 26L more. How much water is in the tank now?
If 4 measuring cups make 1 litre, how much is 2 measuring cups?
questions.hint: 2 cups is half of 4 cups, so it is half a litre.

questions.prompt: A jug holds 2L and a bottle holds 3L. How many litres do they hold altogether? (write like 5L or 5)
